chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him being asked about a man who bought a bondwoman and then had relations with her before ensuring her womb was clear. He said: “How evil is what he did. He should seek forgiveness from Allah and not repeat it.”

He said: Then if he sold her to another man, and he had relations with her without ensuring her womb was clear, then the second sold her to another man, and he had relations with her without ensuring her womb was clear, and her pregnancy became apparent while she was with the third, then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The child belongs to the bed, and for the fornicator is the stone.”

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: having no legal right or claim in this context
key_terms.الْعَاهِرِ: the fornicator or one with no lawful claim
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: the child is legally attributed to the established marital or ownership bed
key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a female bondwoman who has been purchased
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا: her womb, whose state must be verified
key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئَ: to observe istibrāʾ by ensuring the womb is clear before relations
key_terms.يَسْتَغْفِرُ: he seeks forgiveness from Allah for the wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on relations with a bondwoman before istibrāʾ, and to whom is the child attributed if pregnancy later appears?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on having relations with a purchased bondwoman before istibrāʾ and declares such conduct blameworthy, requiring seeking forgiveness and not returning to it. It also establishes the rule of attribution of the child in a case of disputed paternity: the child is assigned to the firāsh, while illicit claim has no legal standing.
